script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for November 12. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Public speaking terrifies people, but it's not dangerous.  Meanwhile, sugar quietly damages health without triggering fear.  Our threat detection is miscalibrated for modern life.

We evolved to fear predators, heights, snakes. We didn't evolve to fear cars, sugar, inactivity. Our threat radar was calibrated for a world that no longer exists. Real dangers are often boring: chronic stress, poor diet, insufficient exercise, financial neglect.  They don't trigger alarm because they're gradual and familiar.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Not everything that feels dangerous is; not everything that is dangerous feels threatening.  Learn to distinguish real threats.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Threat Calibration - What's Really Dangerous?.

Here's your activity: List what you fear. List what actually endangers you (health, finances, relationships). Compare the lists. Where is fear misaligned with threat? Recalibrate your threat detection to reality. This helps you distinguish real threats from perceived ones.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about recognizing real threats can be applied to threat calibration - what's really dangerous?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
